q: On what basis does the Turing Test judge whether a machine is intelligent?
options: Whether a human judge can no longer tell it apart from a person
Whether it reasons internally in the same way a human brain does
Whether it can process information faster than a human can
Whether it was built using biologically inspired methods
explain: A machine passes when a judge cannot tell its replies from a person's. The test looks only at behaviour, so how the machine works, its speed or brain-like design does not matter.

options: It aims to be indistinguishable from the human mind
It is already in everyday use in chatbots and phones
It is designed to solve one specific problem only
It would be able to plan for the future and be creative
It would have self-awareness and consciousness
explain: Strong AI is a theoretical goal, a machine with human-level intelligence. Systems in everyday use are narrow weak AI.

q: A chess program always returns the same move for the same board and keeps no memory of earlier games. Which type of AI is this?
options: A reactive machine
A limited memory machine
A theory of mind system
A self-aware system
explain: Reactive machines have no memory and are task specific, so an input always gives the same output. Deep Blue is the standard example.

q: Which of these are among the four types of AI, ordered from simple to advanced?
options: Self-awareness
Weak AI
Limited memory machines
Reactive machines
Theory of mind
Strong AI
explain: Weak and strong AI are a separate split, based on how broad the ability is. The four types are ordered by memory and understanding.

q: A system reaches intelligent behaviour by a method that looks nothing like human thought. From the behavioural view of AI, is this a problem?
options: Yes, because only biologically observable methods count as AI
Yes, because the method must match how humans reason
No, but only if the system also has consciousness
No, because the outcome matters and the method does not
explain: In a computing context what matters is the behaviour produced. The definition of AI does not have to be confined to biologically observable methods.

q: Explain what the Turing Test is and how a computer passes it.
model: The Turing Test is a way of defining AI by behaviour instead of asking whether a machine can really think. A human judge communicates with a hidden entity and has to decide whether it is a computer or a person. If the judge cannot tell, the computer passes and is said to be intelligent. The test cares about the outcome, so it ignores how the machine produces its answers. It replaced the hard question of whether machines think with a question that can be tested.
points: It tests whether a machine can show intelligent behaviour equal to a human
A human judge cannot tell if the other entity is a computer
If the judge fails to tell, the computer has passed and counts as intelligent
It focuses on behaviour and not on intellect or how the machine works

q: Compare weak AI and strong AI and give one example of weak AI.
model: Weak AI is built to solve a specific problem using predefined instructions and parameters. It does not cover the full range of human cognitive ability. Almost all of today's AI is weak, for example Siri, Alexa or a self driving car. Strong AI would match human intelligence, with self awareness, consciousness, creativity and the ability to plan for the future. It exists only as a theoretical idea with today's technology, so no real system is an example.
points: Weak AI solves limited specific problems
Strong AI would equal human intelligence and have self awareness
Gives one correct example of weak AI, such as a voice assistant or chatbot
Strong AI only exists as a theoretical concept today

q: Describe the four types of AI and say which one does not exist yet.
model: The four types run from simple to advanced. Reactive machines have no memory and give fixed outputs. Limited memory machines learn from data and look at the past. Theory of mind AI would understand human motives and intentions and predict behaviour, and it would be broad rather than limited to one domain. Self aware AI would have a conscious sense of its own existence. Self awareness does not exist yet because we do not know enough about the human brain and emotion.
points: Names all four types in order
Reactive machines have no memory and limited memory machines learn from past data
Theory of mind understands motives and intentions
Self awareness is a sense of self and does not exist yet
